hypothesis: The measured same-thread fusion was correct at 34.929 ms versus the 35.464 ms baseline, while a one-launch variant using separate block cohorts measured 36.408 ms. This experiment keeps same-thread fusion but cooperatively stages each block's x and gy halo plus filter in shared memory. That should reduce repeated global loads and per-tap bounds checks for the shared-memory-sized path; staging overhead, synchronization, or resource pressure may outweigh the savings. Larger filters use a fused global-memory fallback so correctness does not depend on shared-memory capacity. This candidate has not been measured.
notes: The prior results are controller measurements; no timing or correctness result is yet available for this shared-memory candidate. The weight-gradient kernel and its launch remain unchanged.
transformations: Replace separate forward and input-gradient launches with one fused kernel that accumulates and freshly writes y and gx for each output element.
For filters fitting within the bounded shared-memory allocation, cooperatively stage x and gy tile halos plus the filter; rely on zero-filled halo elements instead of per-tap bounds checks.
Use a fused global-memory path when the shared-memory requirement exceeds 8 KiB, preserving the operation for larger filters without depending on device-specific shared-memory capacity.
